ev: research shows that your brain isn't capable of paying close attention to more than one complex task at a time

ev: But innate activities like walking, chewing, and breathing do not require you to pay attention, whereas activities such as reading, tapping out a text message, or driving a car do require attention.

ev: we might be in great trouble when we try to juggle more than two tasks, simply because we have only two frontal lobes

ev: there might be some truth to the claim that women are superior multi-taskers

ev: Strayer thinks that pilots of high-performance aircraft, high-end chefs who can cook several meals at the same time to perfection, and elite doctors in hospital emergency rooms might all be more likely to be super-taskers.
18.why: Section E: phi công, đầu bếp hàng đầu, bác sĩ cấp cứu giỏi có thể là 'siêu đa nhiệm' → i (Professions in which super-taskers are likely to be found).

ev: The ability to multi-task probably comes down to the DNA you inherit from your parents to a large extent, says Strayer.

ev: These so-called 'super-taskers' exhibit different patterns of brain activity when multi-tasking compared to ordinary people

ev: Strayer's research shows that performance deteriorates drastically when attention is split between tasks: more mistakes are made

ev: Psychiatrist Edward M Hallowell even describes multi-tasking as 'a mythical activity in which people believe they can perform two or more tasks simultaneously

ev: 'You are either born with the neural structure that allows you to overcome the usual multi-tasking challenges, or you aren't.
